title: pvPCANormalEstimation
body:
## pvPCANormalEstimation

Estimates a normal at every point of a polydata point cloud by principal component analysis: a plane is fitted to each point's neighbours and its normal is stored in the point array PCANormals. Use it for scanned or particle data without connectivity, where surface normals cannot be computed from polygons (use normals or pvGenerateSurfaceNormals for meshed surfaces). The neighbourhood is chosen by SearchMode, SampleSize and Radius; the sign of each normal is arbitrary unless NormalOrientation fixes it.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- With the ParaView default orientation As Computed, neighbouring normals can point to opposite sides of the surface; choose Point or Graph Traversal when shading or offsets depend on a consistent side.
- Input must be polydata; convert other datasets with pvConvertToPointCloud first.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `PCANormalEstimation`. Identity: `filters/PCANormalEstimation`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input from which the normals are estimated. Accepted data: polygonal data (surfaces, lines or vertices) (vtkPolyData). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPolyData"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FlipNormals` | Flip the normals. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `NormalOrientation` | Orientation mode of the normals. | `{"type":"enum","values":["As Computed","Point","Graph Traversal"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"As Computed"` |
| `OrientationPoint` | Point used to orient the normals. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `Radius` | Radius of the sphere to use for the search of nearest neighbors. | `{"minimum":0.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.0` |
| `SampleSize` | Number of points to sample for PCA. | `{"minimum":0,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0` |
| `SearchMode` | Configure how the filter selects the neighbor points used to calculate the PCA. With KNN mode K (SampleSize) points are selected regardless of their location relative to the sampled point. The radius can also be set to ensure that a sufficiently large neighborhood is taken into account, if not (i.e. all points fall inside the radius), the second approach is performed. With Radius mode, neighboring points are selected inside a radius (RADIUS), only the neighborhood of the sampled point is considered. If K (SampleSize) is also set, the number of points found inside the radius must be larger than K, if not the first approach is performed. Both approaches give the same results. The first approach is faster for uniform point clouds, in other cases, the second approach is faster. | `{"type":"enum","values":["KNN","Radius"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"KNN"` |
